purpose: Contemporaneous IAS corrections and near-stall overlap audit for US WWII fighters; the numerical curves are primary-source anchors, not extrapolated stall calibrations.

sources.report: Pilots Handbook of Flight Operating Instructions AN 01-45HA-1, 15 March 1945
sources.location: printed pp.39-40 stall table; p.45 Section III.1 airspeed-position-error table
sources.instrument_calibration: Manual explicitly assumes zero instrument scale error; not actual proof of zero error.

sources.report: USN Grumman Pilots Handbook of Flight Operating Instructions for Navy F6F-3/-3N/-5/-5N
sources.location: printed p.47, scan PDF page 44 (1-based), Figures 38 and 38a
sources.speed_basis_warning: The figures say IAS and airspeed correction, not explicitly CAS; calibrated result is the conventional interpretation, not a source quotation.

sources.location: VI.A airspeed indicator and altimeter calibration table, explicitly labelled calibrated airspeed
V.B Airspeed Calibration, IAS corrected for instrument error versus CAS

sources.report: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Flight Operating Instructions, 5 April 1944
sources.location: printed pp.25 (Figs.24-25 IAS stalls) and 29 (airspeed correction chart)
original Fig.1 position correction; stall table V.E

sources.report: USN NAS Patuxent final flight report, Figure 3 revised 24 October 1944
sources.location: scan PDF p.23 Figure 3, Airspeed Indicator Calibration
sources.note: 'True Indicated Airspeed' output is NOT unambiguously certified CAS, position/installation error may remain. This chart therefore is not an IAS->CAS curve.

calibration_curves.source_location: printed p.45, Section III.1, Clean Condition
calibration_curves.notes: The manufacturer explicitly calls this PITOT POSITION ERROR and assumes zero instrument scale error; CAS* is conditional on that assumption. Flaps up; gear not specified by chart, conventionally clean/gear up. Do not automatically correct independent USN trial mph figures with unspecified speed basis.

calibration_curves.source_location: printed p.45, Section III.1, Landing Condition
calibration_curves.notes: Manufacturer explicitly calls PITOT POSITION ERROR and assumes zero instrument scale error. Full landing flaps 50 degrees for direct original stall overlap; 20/30-degree partial flaps were NOT separately calibrated, so no automatic transfer to those stalls.
Manual says IAS + correction, not explicitly CAS; conventional interpretation. All available USN F6F-3 stall figures are below the 100-knot minimum of this chart. No extrapolation.

calibration_curves.source_location: original Fig.38a, p.47, right-hand table: FLAPS RETRACTED
calibration_curves.notes: Original F6F-5 has NEGATIVE low-speed IAS correction, unlike F6F-3, demonstrating unsafe variant transfer. Minimum chart speed 100kt exceeds available F6F-5 test stall values.
Flap angle and landing gear state unspecified by this chart; do not assume full-flaps gear-down CAS at stall. Listed F6F-5 landing minimum speeds ~79-84.5 mph (about 69-73kt), BELOW chart 80kt.

calibration_curves.source_location: VI.A, three explicit columns raw IAS, water-column and calibrated IAS
calibration_curves.notes: Original water-column instrument-error results at IAS 150/180/210/240/270/300/330/360 were 151.5/182/212/242/272/301.5/331.5/361 mph respectively; IAS->CAS shown already includes both corrections. P-38J 42-67869 stalls 53-99mph and cannot be corrected from this high-speed chart.

Underlying water-column instrument values 170.5,201,230,260,290.5,311.5 mph; combined IAS->CAS values are source's explicit calibrated mph. Flap/gear configuration during this calibration not independently documented. P-47B measured stalls 88-108mph, no overlap.

Input is explicitly IAS ALREADY CORRECTED FOR INSTRUMENT ERROR. Cannot convert raw cockpit IAS without separate instrument calibration; source says auxiliary-tank configurations differ less than 1mph from reference.

Original calls output 'Calibrated Indicated Airspeed'. No configuration-specific low speed chart; original P-51D manual on p.25 warns stalls read ~10mph HIGHER IAS than preceding P-51 models due to changed airspeed system. Never use this correction for 80-110mph stalls.

observations.source_location: printed p.40, Section II para.16(a)(3), 11,300lb 178USgal fuel and 1200 ammunition rounds
observations.notes: Raw handbook indicated stalling speed. Manufacturer p.45 position-correction table is applicable in-range if instrument scale error assumed zero. This is an operating manual figure, not a documented single airframe flight-test repeat.
NO corrected CAS*: 87kt raw IAS lies below clean correction table minimum of 90kt; do not extrapolate.
NO corrected CAS*: 84kt IAS below 90kt clean correction limit.
NO corrected CAS*: 66kt IAS below 70kt full-flap correction minimum.
NO corrected CAS*: full landing flaps and 30-degree flaps not explicitly shown to share the same position correction curve.
NO corrected CAS*: 20-degree partial flap not specifically calibrated; landing curve applied only to full 50-degree flap in this pack.

uncertainties: instrument error not independently measured: the original p45 manual explicitly ASSUMES zero scale error
handbook stall is an operational representative weight point, not a recorded single-airframe test repeat
flap calibration caption says landing flaps down; 50-degree full flaps taken from matched original landing stall configuration

blocked_low_speed_audits.why: No observed original position-error data at 67.5-86mph; instrument error to be reconciled separately. Do not extrapolate the drawn Fig.1.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Original Eng-47-1734-A references Fig.1 and Fig.2, but no low-speed numeric figure audited

Manual warns P-51D raw IAS stalling speeds ~10mph higher than previous Mustangs due airspeed-system change, not physical wing change; table cannot be extrapolated to stalls.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Report VI.A IAS-to-CAS table 150-360mph; original stall table expressly IAS corrected for instrument error ONLY
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: No measured pitot-static position calibration at stalls and input IAS status differs from raw indicated instrument reading.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Eng-47-1771-A refers to Fig.1 position-error curve, not transcribed with verified near-stall points
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: Figure unavailable for exact near-stall digitization; never borrow 42-67869 installation chart.
No low-speed overlap and no reliable flap/gear matching.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Eng-47-1774-A explicitly says uncorrected ship indicator; Fig.1 position correction not available as audited numeric low-speed points
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: Do not borrow P-47B or N pitot installation curves.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Report V.B 120-300mph instrument-corrected IAS to CAS
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: Original lowest point 120mph and no source-matched stall speed in this pack; raw IAS requires separate instrument calibration.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: Original F6F manual tables: F6F-3 clean >=100kt; F6F-5 clean >=100kt, flaps extended >=80kt
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: Known trials' 76-100.5mph (~66-87kt) mostly below minimum correction speed; their NAS minimum-speed mph basis is also unspecified. F6F-3 and F6F-5 correction signs differ!

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: 1944 flight test Fig.3 'Airspeed Indicator Calibration' plots indicated versus 'TRUE INDICATED'; original manual gives other representative-airframe position corrections
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: Report flight-test minimum speeds are 'MPH' basis unspecified, flight-test stall airplane identified 02158 but calibration Fig3 labels 02155, and 'true indicated' is not proof both position and instrument errors were removed. Manual correction cannot be silently substituted.

blocked_low_speed_audits.calibration: 1948 Navy trial explicitly reports calibrated airspeed at stall in knots
blocked_low_speed_audits.why: No IAS conversion needed; a postwar test of a WWII model; landing fourth-row duplicate power-on label remains a separate provenance ambiguity.

ingestion_rules: Only use original table anchor intervals; never extrapolate below first or above last anchor.
Match individual airframe/test source or explicitly documented model-manual transfer; do not mix F6F-3 with F6F-5 or P-47B/D/N.
Do not infer a reported mph-only test result was IAS merely because a correction table exists.

Distinguish raw IAS, instrument-error-corrected IAS, CAS, EAS, and 'true indicated' in historical usage; both component corrections must be traceable to claim true CAS, and an assumed-zero instrument error yields provisional CAS* only.
Flap angles, gear states and power effects must match. Unknown calibration configurations do not match other source observations.

The Corsair single CAS* is conditioned on original March 1945 manual zero-scale-error assumption, but is not an independently measured instrument correction; retain the asterisk in simulator labels and scorecards.
